rules.rule: Rulebook changes go only through go:review, never hand-edited
must: Change the rules only through `go:review`
never hand-edit them
adding or changing a rule belongs to go:review

rules.rule: Reference mode applies Production to .go and Test to _test.go; Test inherits Production
must: apply the Production section to `\*\.go` and the Test section to `\*_test\.go`
Test inherits Production unless a Test rule overrides it
before editing a `\*_test\.go` file,\s+read `references/test\.md` and `references/production\.md` both
Wrap errors with `%w` and add context; never swallow the error
never `==`

rules.rule: Library functions never write to stdout/stderr
must: Never write output \(errors included\) to stdout/stderr from library

rules.rule: Production reads env vars via ring, never os.Getenv
must: reads it via `rng\.EnvGet`/`EnvLookup`; never `os\.Getenv`

rules.rule: Tests set env vars via rng.EnvSet, never t.Setenv
must: Set an environment variable for code under test with `rng\.EnvSet`, never `t\.Setenv`

rules.rule: Multi-line string literals are segmented with +, never raw backticks
must: never use a raw backtick string for multi-line content
joined with `\+`

rules.rule: Tests use Given/When/Then markers; single action under When
must: `--- Given ---` arranges, `--- When ---` performs the single action under test
never move the call under test out of `--- When ---`

rules.rule: have/want never got; t.Context never context.Background
must: Name the actual value `have` and the expected value `want`, never `got`
Use `t\.Context\(\)`, never `context\.Background\(\)`

rules.rule: Never add production overrides only for a test
must: never add a production override \(env var, hook, parameter\) only so a test can reach a branch

rules.rule: Rule edits redirect to go:review, unknown targets ask
must: redirect to `go:review`

rules.rule: plan_first proposes then stops; checks nothing
must: propose the budget and the package list, then stop for the
checking nothing until it comes

rules.rule: A token that is no control, mode, or target is named as unrecognized and the run uses the defaults; an unresolvable target asks
must: say it was not recognized, name the ones that exist, and run with the defaults as if it were absent
A target that resolves to nothing: say so and ask — never guess what to work on

rules.rule: The module's .editorconfig is read before the first edit
must: Before that first edit, read the module's `\.editorconfig`
else 80 and 4

rules.rule: A pass without fix changes no file, so a dropped control never widens it
must: A pass without `fix` changes no file, so a dropped control never widens\s+it
